units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 123:2">Targ. Ps. CXXIII, 2</cite> <he>מודיקין … מ׳ וכ׳</he> looking out for (the remnant of) a dish at the hands of their masters (in ed. Wil. our w. omitted); <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 11:6">Targ. Y. Num. XI, 6</cite> (not <he>דמוריק</he>).—

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 28:2">Lev. R. s. 28</cite> <he>כיון דהוה מ׳ עליל</he> whenever a dish was brought in; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 28:2">ib.</cite> <he>וכיון דמְגוּסִי עליל</he> as soon as a dish of mine comes in; (<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 1:3">Koh. R. to I, 3</cite> <cite ref="V00079"><he>תבשילא</he></cite>).—Pl. <he>מְגִיסִין</he>, <he>מְגִיסַיָּא</he>, <cite ref="M00167"><he>מְגוּ׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 4:7">Targ. O. Num. IV, 7</cite> (ed. Amst. <cite ref="M00204"><he>מַגִּי׳</he></cite>); a. fr.—

Targ. Ez. XIII, 19 מגוסין דלחם (not מנ׳; ed. Lag. מְגוּסְיָין) plates with morsels from the tables (h. text פתותי).—Lev. R. l. c. למה מגו׳ נפקין וכ׳ why are the plates carried out without having been tasted?—2 (= Lat. accubatio) dinner, banquet.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 1:3:1">Koh. R. to I, 3</cite> <he>דבגין מְגִיסָךְ אתית</he> that I came for the sake of thy dinner.
